newsitem.title: SYRIA: Syrian paper says Netanyahu closing door for peace.
newsitem.headline: Syrian paper says Netanyahu closing door for peace.

text.p: An official Syrian newspaper on Sunday said Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's vow to never give up the Golan Heights meant there can be no peace talks.
"This obstinate position would close the doors for efforts which are supposed to start again with the begining of the second term of office of U.S. President Bill Clinton," the daily al-Baath said.

Damascus wants Israel to return all the Golan Heights, captured by Israel from Syria in the 1967 Middle East war. Sporadic peace talks between Syria and Israel, which began in 1991, did not resolve the issue.
Al-Baath said Netanyahu's refusal to discuss return of the Golan, published by the French daily Le Figaro on Saturday, "reflects a new phase of provocations and pressures (against Syria)."
President Clinton, whose country is sponsoring the Arab-Israeli peace talks that began in 1991, will start his second term on Monday.

In the first direct Syrian comment on the Israeli-Palestinian deal on a partial Israeli withdrawal from the West Bank town of Hebron, al-Baath said the agreement gave Israel big gains and allowed Netanyahu's Likud party to appear as a peace-maker.
"There should be a swift Arab action to counter the Likud obstinacy which is trying to utilise the Hebron deal to beautify its image and to appear as a peace-maker," al-Baath said.

Netanyahu, who last week signed the long-delayed deal on Hebron, told Le Figaro that Israel and Syria were inching toward talks. But he ruled out any negotiation on ending the occupation of East Jerusalem or the Golan Heights.

"Netanyahu's remarks, in which he renewed his adherence to the occupation of the Golan and Jerusalem, means that the redeployment (in Hebron), with all the gains that Israel got, is considered by Netanyahu as the end of the peace process," the newspaper said.
Israel's previous Labour-led government, defeated in May elections by Netanyahu, broke off talks with Syria last March after Islamic suicide bombings in Israel killed 59 people.
Al-Baath said Syria would never accept a return to peace talks unless Israel "clearly and completely commits itself to withdrawal from the Golan to (pre-war) June 4, 1967 lines."
"Any other talks would be nonsense," al-Baath said.
